title: fix(app-shell): scope the metadata seed cache to the active organization
body:
Fixes #4486

`MetadataProvider` seeds its app list from `sessionStorage` before the org-scoped fetch returns, under a key built from the metadata **type alone** (`objectui:metadata:app`). `sessionStorage` is per-tab and survives the full-page navigation the workspace switcher performs, so after an org switch every `useMetadata().apps` consumer in the seed window read the **previous org's** list. Separately, a cached `[]` is truthy, so an empty cached list also cleared `initialLoading`.

## Premise re-measured

Re-verified against `origin/main` before editing; the card (filed 2026-08-12, re-triaged 2026-08-17) is accurate and the provider has not been restructured.

- `loadFromSession('app')` read `SESSION_STORAGE_PREFIX + type` — no org component.
- `WorkspaceSwitcher.handleSwitch` awaits `switchOrganization` (which writes `ActiveOrganizationStorage`) and then sets `window.location.href = resolveRootUrl()`, so the next mount sees the **new** org id and the **same** `sessionStorage`.
- The seed effect's `if (cached)` accepted `[]` and called `setInitialLoading(false)`.

The card's "any other consumer inherits the same wrong answer" is literal: about 15 surfaces read `useMetadata().apps` — `AppSidebar`, `UnifiedSidebar`, `AppSwitcher`, `AppHeader`, `SearchResultsPage`, `InboxPopover`, `HomePage`, `AiChatPage`, `useNavigationSync`, `AppContent`, `ConsoleShell` among them. `RootLandingRedirect` was simply the one that got caught.

## The fix

- **Scope the seed key by the active org**, read from `ActiveOrganizationStorage`. That is deliberately the same value `createAuthenticatedFetch` stamps as `X-Tenant-ID` on the `/api/v1/meta/*` request that fills the cache, so the cache scope equals the tenant the server actually filtered the list for and the two cannot drift apart. It is deliberately **not** `useAuth().activeOrganization?.id`: that resolves asynchronously after mount, so at seed time it is still `null` and every boot would miss its own entry.
- **A cached empty list is a miss.** No seed, `initialLoading` stays true until the fetch lands. Seeding zero items saved no render and the `status: 'ready'` it stamped made `getTypeStatus('app')` claim a settled answer the provider did not have.
- **The pre-fix unscoped entry is deleted on first read** rather than left inert in storage for the life of the tab — see the upgrade question below.
- **An org change with no reload drops the in-memory cache** (details next).

### Why the in-memory half is in scope, not scope creep

The card's ruled fix is "include the active org identifier in the storage key **(or invalidate on org change)**". Both were needed, because keying the storage only covers the switch paths that reload.

`packages/app-shell/src/console/organizations/manage/OrganizationLayout.tsx` calls `switchOrganization` from an effect whenever the `/organizations/:slug` segment names a different org, with **no navigation at all**:

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (org && activeOrganization?.id !== org.id) {
    switchOrganization(org.id).catch(...);
  }
}, [org, activeOrganization, switchOrganization]);
```

On that path the storage key never comes into play — the live in-memory cache is what answers `useMetadata().apps`, and it would keep serving the previous org's items until the 5-minute TTL lapsed. That is exactly the "a re-keying that still serves stale data by some other path" failure, so the invariant is enforced where the data lives rather than at the key. That file is **not** touched by this PR (it is outside the declared region); the guard is entirely inside `MetadataProvider`.

Two details that the mechanism forces:

- The clear also **re-arms the `app` fetch**. `apps` is read straight off the entry (`getEntry('app').items`) rather than through `readType`, so unlike every lazy type it is not re-armed by a consumer reading it; without the kick the clear would leave the nav permanently empty on the no-reload path. `initialLoading` goes back up for the same reason cached-empty is a miss.
- The **first resolution** of the active org (unknown to known) is deliberately not treated as a switch. `AuthProvider` resolves the membership list asynchronously, so `null` to an id happens on every normal boot; clearing there would discard the eager `app`/`object`/`view` fetches mid-flight and refetch all three — the request-budget regression pinned by objectui#4042. Pinned by its own test.

## Privacy: are any cached fields org-confidential?

Asked explicitly by triage. Answering by enumeration.

**What the cache holds.** Only the `app` metadata type — application *definitions* per `AppSchema` (`@objectstack/spec`): `name`, `label`, `description`, `icon`, `branding` (colours, logo/favicon URLs), `active` / `isDefault` / `hidden` / `_unpublished`, the `navigation` tree, `areas`, `contextSelectors` (including `optionsSource.endpoint` and filter values), `requiredPermissions` (permission-set names), `defaultAgent`, and the `_lock*` / `_provenance` / `_packageId` / `_packageVersion` provenance keys.

**What it does not hold.** No record rows, no field values, no user or member data, no credentials. The bearer token lives under a separate `localStorage` key (`auth-session-token`) and the active-org id under `auth-active-organization-id`; neither is in this cache.

**Is any of it org-scoped?** Yes, in the *configuration-disclosure* sense rather than the customer-data sense. `_provenance: 'org'` is a real value, so an app definition can be workspace-authored; for such an app the `navigation` tree, `requiredPermissions` and `contextSelectors.optionsSource.endpoint` describe that tenant's private data model and permission naming. The list is also **per-user**: the server filters `GET /api/v1/meta/:type` per session (`filterAppForUser`, objectstack#8013), so the entry is "the apps that user could see in that org".

**Was it being served across a tenant boundary — i.e. does this need a maintainer severity call?** On the path this card is about, **no**, and that is why this stayed a keying fix rather than a `needs_decision`. `sessionStorage` is per-origin **and per-tab**, so nothing here is readable by another machine or another tab. The reader on the org-switch path is the **same signed-in user**, and the org list they can switch between is their own membership list (`setActiveOrganization` is server-gated). They were legitimately authorised to read org A's app list seconds earlier. No principal gains access to anything they were not already entitled to — this is wrong data driving decisions plus a tenant-isolation hygiene defect, not a privilege escalation.

**On the upgrade question:** because the exposure is bounded to the tab and to a user who held both memberships, re-keying going forward would have been sufficient. The old unscoped entry is deleted anyway on the first read — it is inert once nothing reads that key, but leaving another org's app list sitting in storage for the life of the tab is not worth defending, and deleting it costs one line.

**One adjacent gap this does not cover, filed separately as #5198.** `signOut` clears only `TokenStorage`; it clears neither the `objectui:metadata:*` entries nor `ActiveOrganizationStorage`, and no sign-out call site reloads. So a *different* user signing into the same tab **and the same org** is still seeded from the previous user's permission-filtered list — a genuine cross-principal case that org-keying cannot close, since two users in one org produce the same key. Out of this card's ruled scope and left untouched here; #5198 carries the detail.

## Tests

New: `packages/app-shell/src/providers/__tests__/MetadataProvider.orgScopedCache.test.tsx` (6 tests).

The invariant is stated about the **data**, not the key: nothing asserts the key format, the cache is filled by *running the provider*, and every assertion reads what a consumer actually gets back. A re-keying that still served stale items by another path would fail these.

| Test | Pins |
| --- | --- |
| never serves the previous org's list in the seed window | the card's invariant |
| still seeds instantly when the org is unchanged | counter-pin: deleting the cache would satisfy the others |
| cached EMPTY list is a miss for `initialLoading` | the truthy-empty half, pinned separately |
| pre-fix unscoped entry is dropped, not served | the upgrade path |
| in-memory cache dropped on a no-reload org change | the `OrganizationLayout` path |
| `null` to id does **not** clear | the objectui#4042 request budget |

**Reverse verification** (fix committed first, then `git checkout origin/main -- MetadataProvider.tsx`, then restored from the branch). The provider and its dependencies resolve through vitest's source aliases (`@object-ui/auth` and friends map to `packages/*/src`), so no `dist` is involved and no rebuild is needed for the ablation to bind. Predicted red before running; observed exactly that, 4 red / 2 green:

```
× never serves the previous org's app list in the seed window after a switch
    AssertionError: expected 'setup,crm' to be ''
× treats a cached EMPTY list as a miss for the initialLoading decision
    AssertionError: expected 'false' to be 'true'
× drops the pre-fix unscoped entry instead of serving it to whichever org mounts next
    AssertionError: expected 'other_org_app' to be ''
× drops the in-memory cache when the active org changes with NO reload
    AssertionError: expected [ 'app' ] to have a length of 2 but got 1
Tests  4 failed | 2 passed (6)
```

The two that stayed green are the counter-pins, which describe behaviour that already existed — the expected direction.

Green runs, with the sha each was measured at:

- `666175e3b` (the commit carrying the whole source change) — full `packages/app-shell/` suite: **436 files, 4211 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed**.
- `731af7004` (after merging `origin/main`) — `packages/app-shell/src/providers/` **7 files, 50 passed**; `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` exit 0 (the script name is echoed in the output, so it really ran rather than matching zero scripts). Gates: `check:control-bytes` OK (4615 files), `check:phantom-deps` OK (this one validates that the new `@object-ui/auth` import is declared by app-shell), `check:self-import` OK. `eslint` on both changed files: 0 errors, and the warning count on `MetadataProvider.tsx` is unchanged at 50 versus the same file on `origin/main`, so no new lint debt.
- `3cf409948` (**final head** — adds only the changeset file, which the source commit had omitted) — changeset gates re-run on the new head: `check-changeset-presence` OK (3 files changed, 2 under a released package's `src/`, 1 changeset), `check-changeset-no-major` OK, `check-changeset-fixed` OK, `check:control-bytes` OK (4616 files).

The full app-shell suite was not re-run after the merge: the merge brought in a sibling's unrelated files (approval-override work under `utils/` and `views/`), the shared verify lock had two other agents queued behind me, and CI runs the four shards on the merged tree regardless.

## Scope

Only `packages/app-shell/src/providers/MetadataProvider.tsx` plus its new test and a changeset. The declared out-of-region paths (`console/**`, `views/**`, `hooks/**`, `utils/**`) are untouched. objectui#4522 (`AppContent`'s `missingRecheck` — different layer, different cache) and PR #4483's bounce are both out of scope and neither was needed.

Changeset: `@object-ui/app-shell` patch.
